items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: The only addition to our band at that time was Herbie Haymer, who was quite a saxophone player. He was working with she and Red Norver.

ctx.x: That escaped me. I can't remember, and I have some --- I'm sure I have quite a few of the 78's at home. Maybe it'll come to me just a little later. But any way I did quite a few recordings with Mildred, as a matter of fact I recorded with Mildred in Chicago before I left Chicago to go to New York. She used to come to the Three Deuces all

the time, and she loved the band, and she recorded with our band. The only addition to our band at that time was Herbie Haymer, who was quite a saxophone player. He was working with she and Red Norver.

We did some tunes, 'Are You Looking At Me,' I can't think of all the tunes but they were very good. And when I went to New York I got in touch with her and we started recording together again. And I recorded as you know, I told you I recorded with Lady Day, did quite a few things with her. One record I did with her was done -- was arranged and conducted by Don Redman, an all star band also. And Georgie Auld, Byas, Don Byas, Roy Eldridge, Kenny Clark, there was just -- and when Kenny didn't make it I think Sid…
